newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Occidental resumes pumping on Colombian pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Occidental resumes pumping on Colombian pipeline.

text.p: Occidental Petroleum Corp said it had resumed pumping along the Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline after repairs to structure were completed early Friday.

A company spokesman cautioned that the pumping operations were "only temporary," however, pending checks for further damage to the line, which leftist guerrillas dynamited on July 10 for the second time in four days.

The spokesman, Robert Stewart, said repair work concluded at 7:21 a.m. local time (1221 GMT) and added that Occidental would know round about noon whether it could totally renew transportation from the Cano Limon field to the Caribbean port of Covenas.

Once that determination is made, and barring any further damage to the pipeline, Stewart said it would take about a day to evacuate the 550,000 barrels of crude oil in storage at Cano Limon and restart production at the field, which has been shut in since July 10.
He said he was unable to comment on how soon force majuere on the field, declared Tuesday, would be lifted, however.
A spokesman for the state oil company Ecopetrol, whose workers moved in to repair the stricken pipeline Thursday afternoon, said all systems appeared to be go after work was completed early Friday.
"If there are no more problems crude should be flowing into Covenas in about six hours," he said.
